Qualtrics M01-1: Designing a Survey

Rough Draft and Sharing Qualtrics

Author

Yujia Luo

NoteAssignment scope

This assignment includes a rough draft of the survey Survey of Educational Needs for MR Professionals, organized into five blocks, and shared with the instructor. The final assignment instructions specify 56 total questions and the following block structure:

Block Required questions
Cover Page 2
Market Research Industry and Profession 11
Educational Needs 13
GCMR Program 15
Demographics 15
Total 56

1. Proof of sharing the Qualtrics survey

The saved project must be shared with Jae Jung, Bronco ID jmjung, with edit and results-related permissions required by the course instructions.

Evidence included: saved Qualtrics collaboration screen.

2. Beginning of the Qualtrics survey

The first block should contain the formatted consent/cover page and the market-research experience screener. The refusal path for the consent question and the No path for the experience question must skip to the end of the survey.

Evidence included: saved beginning-of-survey screenshot.

Checks to complete in Preview:

  • Consent = No ends the survey.
  • Worked in a market-research-related profession = No ends the survey.
  • Consent and screener wording is readable and the question numbering is block-based rather than manually typed.

3. Middle of the Qualtrics survey

The middle should show the Educational Needs or GCMR Program block. Q3.2, Q3.3, Q3.4, and Q3.5 must be built as Side by Side questions, with separate researcher and salesperson columns. They must not be replaced by ordinary Matrix questions.

Evidence included: saved middle-of-survey screenshot.

Logic and coding checks include:

Item Required configuration
Q3.2-Q3.5 Side by Side; Very much=3, Somewhat=2, Not at all=1, Don’t know=4; exclude Don’t know from analysis
Q3.7 Display only when Q3.6 includes Master’s Degree; exclude I don’t know from analysis
Q3.9 Display only when Q3.8 includes Master’s Degree; exclude I don’t know from analysis
Q4.5-Q4.7 Very likely=7 through Very unlikely=1
Q4.8 Extremely well=5 through Not at all=1
Q4.9 Display for the three unlikely responses in Q4.5
Q4.10 Very Interested=6 through Very Uninterested=1
Q4.12 Exclude Don’t know from analysis while keeping it selectable

4. Ending of the Qualtrics survey

The last block should contain demographic questions, an essay-sized optional comments question, and a one-line voluntary email question with email validation.

Evidence included: saved ending-of-survey screenshot.

Required display logic in the ending block:

  • Q5.6 displays for Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. education selections.
  • Q5.7 displays for Master’s or Ph.D. selections.
  • Q5.8 displays for Ph.D. selections.
  • Q5.12 displays only for California residents.
  • Q5.13 displays only for Southern California residents.
  • Q5.14 is an Essay question.
  • Q5.15 is a one-line optional email field with email-format validation.

5. Rough-draft progress

The local preparation package contains a 52-question Qualtrics import draft covering all five blocks. Four Educational Needs Side by Side questions (Q3.2-Q3.5) must be created in the Qualtrics editor to reach the required 56 questions. The local draft also contains blank placeholders for Q3.10-Q3.12 and Q4.10 because the source Word survey was not included in the supplied folder; their exact wording must be copied from the course source before final submission.

Functions prepared in the local package:

  • five-block organization and question IDs;
  • answer choices and most response coding;
  • a build guide for skip logic, display logic, validation, reverse coding, and analysis exclusions;
  • the required Side by Side item specifications.

Functions that must be verified in the CPP Qualtrics account:

  • actual import or question-by-question build;
  • completion of all 56 questions and exact wording;
  • saved skip/display logic;
  • Look and Feel and block numbering;
  • sharing with jmjung;
  • Preview testing;
  • four evidence screenshots (included in Sections 1-4 above).
